history.period: Oral tradition says 200+ years old, possibly 18th century
history.summary: CSV town 'Koderma' is the district; the temple actually stands on Chanchal Hill near Domchanch/Satgawan on the Koderma-Giridih highway, about 33 km from Koderma town (town corrected to Domchanch). Perched about 400 feet above ground, the shrine began, in local legend, when a tribal priest found a Durga idol in a cave on the hill. A narrow cave beside the temple holds rock paintings of four Durga forms. It is locally revered as a Shakti Peeth (NOT one of the canonical 51 Shakti Peethas) and blends tribal Sarna rites with Hindu worship: vermilion (sindoor) is prohibited, devotees must bathe before entry, and arwa rice with mishri is offered as prasad. A local trust manages the 3-acre complex (including a Shiva shrine and sacred pond) since 2000, when a staircase was built up the hill.

name: Maa Chanchala Devi Temple (Shaktipeeth)
town_description: Domchanch is a block town in Koderma district on the Koderma-Giridih highway, about 33 km from the district headquarters. Set amid forested hills of the Chota Nagpur plateau, it is best known as the gateway to the Chanchala Devi hill shrine and attracts pilgrims on Tuesdays and Saturdays. The surrounding belt is part of Jharkhand's mica-mining country.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism, blended with tribal Sarna rites)

travel.road: On the Koderma-Giridih highway (SH); reachable by private vehicle/taxi from Koderma or Domchanch via Satgawan/Khorimahua Road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Durga Puja/Navratri for the annual fair
